question.prompt: Real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) are chosen independently and uniformly at random from the interval \((0, 1).\) What is the probability that \(\lfloor \log_2 x \rfloor = \lfloor \log_2 y \rfloor,\) where \(\lfloor r \rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to the real number \(r?\)

solutions.title: Sum matching square areas
solutions.explanation:
Equal floors mean that \(x\) and \(y\) lie between the same two consecutive powers of \(2\).

Since \(0<x<1\), the possible values of \(\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor\) are \(-1,-2,-3,\ldots\). For a positive integer \(n\),
\[
\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor=-n
\iff -n\le\log_2 x<-n+1
\iff 2^{-n}\le x<2^{1-n}.
\]
The last equivalence uses the fact that powers of \(2\) increase with their exponents. The same interval condition holds for \(y\).

Independence and uniform sampling make \((x,y)\) uniformly distributed over the unit square, whose area is \(1\). When both floors equal \(-n\), the favorable pairs form a square of side length
\[
2^{1-n}-2^{-n}=2^{-n},
\]
so its area is \(4^{-n}\).

These squares are disjoint because different values of \(n\) give different floor values, and together they cover every case of equal floors. Boundary points do not affect area or probability. Hence the desired probability is
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{4^n}
=\frac{\frac14}{1-\frac14}
=\boxed{\frac13}.
\]
Here the geometric series converges because its common ratio is \(\frac14<1\). The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
